text.p: Patrick Flatley scored twice and the New York Rangers completed a home-and-home sweep of the Philadelphia Flyers with a 6-3 victory Thursday in a battle of possible first-round playoff opponents.

The Rangers, coming off a 3-2 home win on Monday, stormed to a 3-0 lead midway through the second period and snapped a three-game road losing streak. New York grabbed sole possession of fifth place in the Eastern Conference with 86 points, two ahead of Pittsburgh.
"The win says what we've known all along, that we're a very good team when we play as well as we can," said goaltender Mike Richter, who made 28 saves.
"We've beaten every top team in the league this year and lost to every team, as well. We seem to make our job harder sometimes. But when we set our minds to it, we can beat anybody."

Vaclav Prospal had a goal and an assist for the Flyers, 1-3-1 in their last five games. Philadelphia remained two points behind New Jersey for the top seed in the Eastern Conference with two games remaining, including a showdown with the Devils in Sunday's season finale.

"Start with disappointing," said Flyers winger Shjon Podein. "It was a night we really wanted to come out with a lot of energy and emotion. We didn't rise to the challenge tonight and it's disappointing."

The Flyers played without All-Star centre Eric Lindros, who served the first game of his two-game suspension. New York was without All-Star centre Mark Messier, who remained sidelined with a charleyhorse.

Lindros was suspended for several rough plays in the opener of the home-and-home series and was quoted in published reports that it was time for Philadelphia to target some of the opponents' top stars.

"Eric has a valid point in a lot of his comments," said teammate John LeClair. "He's put up with a lot of stuff on the ice and it's tough. He's a great player and people look for him and go after him. It's tough to play 82 games like that."
Ryan Vandenbussche, Adam Graves, Darren Langdon and Niklas Sundstrom also scored goals, and Mike Eastwood and Wayne Gretzky each had two assists for the Rangers, who won the season series, 3-2-1.
Rod Brind'Amour and Trent Klatt tallied for Philadelphia.

In Boston, the Buffalo Sabres clinched their first division title in 16 years as Miroslav Satan scored twice, including one that capped a three-goal burst in an 85-second span of the second period, in a 5-1 win over the Bruins.
The Sabres, who got 27 saves from Dominik Hasek, shook off a 1-6-1 slide to close out the Northeast Division title, their first divisional crown since 1980-81, when they won the Adams.
Derek Plante, Darryl Shannon and Randy Burridge also scored for the Sabres, who broke an 0-4-1 road slide and sent Boston to the brink of securing the league's worst record.
Jason Allison had the only goal but missed a penalty shot for the Bruins, who lost for the ninth time in 10 games. They dropped all five meetings with the Sabres this season, scoring just five times.
In St. Louis, Harry York had a career-high three points on two goals and an assist as the Blues scored a 5-1 victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs.
York, who had been scratched for five of the previous six games, recorded his first-ever two-goal game.
Jon Casey stopped 16 shots for his first win in more than two months.

Scott Pellerin and Stephane Matteau each had a goal and an assist for St. Louis, which moved into a fifth-place tie with Phoenix and Edmonton in the West. The Blues close the regular season Sunday at Detroit.
Felix Potvin appeared in his league-high 73rd game, but was pulled following the second period after allowing three goals on 17 shots. Toronto dropped to 0-3-1 in its last four contests.

At Tampa Bay, Dino Ciccarelli scored with 4:56 left in the third period to snap a tie and Corey Schwab stopped all 17 shots he faced in a relief role as the Lightning edged the Pittsburgh Penguins 4-3, keeping their playoff hopes alive.
Rob Zamuner, Chris Gratton and Paul Ysebaert also tallied for Tampa Bay, which is unbeaten in three straight (2-0-1).
The victory moved the Lightning (72 points) within one point of the Ottawa Senators and Hartford Whalers, who are tied for the eighth and final playoff spot in the Eastern Conference.

At Washington, Joe Juneau took advantage of a 5-on-3 power play to score what proved to be the game-winner in the second period and the Capitals kept their playoff hopes alive with a 3-2 victory over the Montreal Canadiens.
The win lifted the Capitals -- who have 71 points -- within two points of final playoff slot in the East.
Montreal is seventh with 76 points and needs only a tie at home against Philadelphia in Saturday's season finale to clinch a post-season berth.
